Push Pull Legs Program

PROGRAM OVERVIEW
Weekly frequency
6 training days
Day structure
Push, pull, legs, repeat
Best for
Intermediate lifters who recover well
Main goal
Balanced hypertrophy and strength practice
WHO IT FITS

A high-frequency split for lifters who can recover

Push Pull Legs works because each training day has a clear job. Push days train pressing muscles, pull days train back and biceps, and leg days collect squat, leg press, hamstring, glute, and calf work.

This MVP page uses the preset LogWise PPL template as the source of truth, so the exercise list below matches the program available inside the app.

WEEKLY LAYOUT

Push, pull, legs, then repeat

Monday Push

Chest, shoulders, triceps

  • Bench Press
  • Overhead Press
  • Lateral Raise
  • Triceps Pushdown
  • Cable Crossover
Tuesday Pull

Back, rear delts, biceps

  • Barbell Row
  • Lat Pulldown
  • Cable Row
  • Biceps Curl
  • Rear Delt Fly
Wednesday Legs

Squat pattern, leg accessories

  • Squat
  • Leg Press
  • Leg Curl
  • Leg Extension
  • Calf Raise
Thursday Push

Second pressing day

  • Dumbell Press
  • Shoulder Press
  • Dumbell Fly
  • Overhead Triceps Extension
Friday Pull

Deadlift and pulling volume

  • Deadlift
  • Pull Up
  • Dumbell Row
  • Hammer Curl
  • Shrug
Saturday Legs

Leg press, lunge, glute work

  • Leg Press
  • Lunge
  • Hip Thrust
  • Leg Curl
  • Calf Raise
Sunday Rest

Recover and review the log

  • Rest or light recovery work
HOW TO PROGRESS

Progress the plan without turning every day into a max test

  • Start with loads you can complete with 1-3 reps in reserve on most working sets.
  • Add reps first, then add weight once all sets reach the top of the target range.
  • Watch weekly volume by movement pattern so push, pull, and legs stay balanced.
  • If performance drops across several sessions, reduce volume or add recovery before adding more exercises.

The workout volume calculator is useful when you want to compare push, pull, and leg workload before changing the split.

What to track

For each exercise, save sets, reps, weight, RIR, and short notes. For the program, review weekly volume and which lifts are moving.
